method: Question-by-question reading of bank 4.0.0 and draft rationales, followed by targeted source cross-checks; no independent human or second-agent review claimed.
scope: Only Nativism and Hansonism; all other drafts and archives preserved.
sourceAccess: Cambridge and Wiley articles, Strathclyde author-repository abstract, One Nation policy pages, ABC reporting and Oxford historical abstract actually read. Oxford Hansonism abstract is labelled as such; failed publisher full-text requests are not represented as full-text reading.

corrections.reason: The current firearms policy retains licensing for farmers, hunters and sporting users under existing strict systems. A separate personal-defence purpose is more likely rejected than introduced; lawful recreational ownership is not the claim asked here.

The doctrine appeals to Judeo-Christian cultural inheritance while defending the constitution’s religious liberty. Keeping inherited culture is not establishing a particular religion as the constitutional foundation of the state. Civil non-establishment is the more likely choice, with symbolic recognition still possible.

The June 2026 speech retains an ABC with some publicly funded regional operations but proposes subscriptions elsewhere and abolishing SBS. Mixed continuing national provision and withdrawal from universal public funding make Neutral more likely than either complete public provision or broadcasting entirely in private hands. This is a substantive hybrid position, not missing evidence.

Restricting foreign ownership of utilities does not choose between domestic private and public ownership. The resource joint-venture model demonstrates selective public participation alongside private firms, making conditional rather than general public ownership most likely.

Opposition to foreign control and support for private domestic enterprise create different judgements depending on the purchaser and service. Neutral expresses that conditional position; a blanket rejection of any private operation is not established.

limits: These are interpreted scoped doctrines, not empirical response distributions.
Nativism is assessed as an electoral cultural variant; host-economic plurality causes substantial uncertainty and conditional Neutral choices.
All 480 answers remain educated assumptions, including choice intensity.
One Nation programme factual and costing claims are treated as policy positions, not validated facts.
Culture–Nature 16 is not clean evidence of heredity; race/IQ/violence premises are not accepted as scientific facts.
